title: Diagnostic envelope
description: The record every error escaping to a process boundary serializes to (DIAG-001). law/DIAG specified this shape in prose from the first release; this file is that specification made machine-readable, so a consuming project can validate against it rather than re-reading the table. NOT YET SELF-ENFORCING: the fitness test DIAG-001 names, `test_envelope_conforms`, is still unbuilt and counted as such in enforce/ENFORCEMENT.md. This file is the contract; nothing in this repository yet proves a producer honours it. The Prime Directive is what every field below serves: an agent meeting a defect determines what broke, where, in which layer, against which contract, with which value, from the program's own output -- and derives the fix without re-reading the codebase.

code.description: Stable, namespaced, greppable (DIAG-002). Lives as a class attribute on the error type, never only in the message text: a code survives message rewording and translation where a sentence does not. Renaming or removing one is a breaking change (DIAG-004, API-011).

layer.description: Where the fault originated (ARCH-001). Derivable rather than guessed, because dependencies point inward and each layer produces only its own error family (ERR-004) -- which is what makes this field worth recording at all.

port.description: Which published contract was crossed. Adapter faults only; absent elsewhere, because there is no contract to name.

operation.description: Which call on that contract. Adapter faults only.

expected.description: The predicate that was violated, stated so a reader can compare it against `actual` (DIAG-003). Structured detail carried as an attribute on the error, not interpolated into a sentence an agent would have to parse back out.

actual.description: What was seen instead. The pair (expected, actual) is the smallest thing from which a fix can be derived without opening the source.

value.description: The offending input, redacted (DIAG-014). Absent rather than null when there is nothing to show; redaction is the producer's obligation and no schema can check it.

rule_ids.description: Discipline rules implicated, by their stable ids. Treated as public API (meta/SCHEMA section 3.1), which is why they may appear in a payload at all.

cause_chain.description: The `__cause__` walk, innermost first (DIAG-005). Present and possibly empty rather than omitted: an empty chain is the claim that nothing was chained, which is different from not having looked. Every cross-layer re-raise chains explicitly, so a gap here is a defect in the producer.

code.description: Its own stable code, where it carries one.

notes.description: Context accreted on the way out via `Exception.add_note` (DIAG-006). Notes rather than re-wrapping, so the original exception and its traceback survive intact.

correlation_id.description: Ties this record to its log lines (DIAG-013). Absent in a process that emits no correlated log.

remediation.description: One line the reader can act on. The field that makes the envelope machine-REPAIRABLE and not merely machine-diagnosable; without it the record says what broke and leaves the next step to be inferred.

allOf.description: An adapter fault names the contract it crossed and the call on it. Anywhere else there is no port to name, so requiring one would force a producer to invent it.
